value: Direct comparisons of ALS and bvFTD revealed minimal gray-matter atrophy in the cerebellum and white-matter changes in the left thalamus in ALS patients. The bvFTD patients showed substantially more significant atrophy in the motor-cortex, striatal, thalamic, and cerebellar areas, as well as in the connecting white-matter tracts between these structures. A particularly notable observation was the absence of significant differences in the brainstem between the two groups.

Contrary to our hypotheses, white-matter structural changes were not greater in ALS patients than in bvFTD patients. Instead, bvFTD patients showed more atrophy across all of the motor-system regions investigated.

definition.value: VBM results for the average SICI revealed that atrophy in the motor cortex covaried with TMS hyperexcitability in ALS. For bvFTD patients, atrophy in the supplementary motor cortex showed the strongest association with hyper-excitability. Cerebellar atrophy was correlated with average SICI in both ALS and bvFTD. Parallel DTI analysis showed correlations with motor-cortex, brainstem, and thalamocerebellar tract white-matter changes in ALS and bilateral corticospinal tract changes at the internal capsule in bvFTD.

value: Atrophy in the motor cortex covaried with TMS hyperexcitability in ALS. For bvFTD patients, atrophy in the supplementary motor cortex showed the strongest association with hyper-excitability, with only a limited involvement of motor-cortex areas. Cerebellar atrophy was correlated with the average SICI score in both the ALS and bvFTD groups.

The average SICI score was significantly correlated with motor-cortex, brainstem, and thalamocerebellar tract white-matter changes in ALS patients, but only with bilateral corticospinal tract changes at the level of the internal capsule in bvFTD patients.
